definitions.explanation: The state of being unhappy or unfortunate.
A polite way to refer to a death in someone's family.

examples.japanese: {不幸|ふこう}な{子供|こども}{時代|じだい}を{過|す}ごした。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{不幸|ふこう}な{結婚|けっこん}{生活|せいかつ}に{苦|くる}しんでいた。
examples.english: She was suffering from an unhappy marriage.

examples.japanese: {お金|かね}があっても{不幸|ふこう}な{人|ひと}はたくさんいる。
examples.english: There are many people who are unhappy even though they have money.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}には{不幸|ふこう}が{続|つづ}いた。
{不幸|ふこう}にも、{事故|じこ}で{大|おお}けがをした。
examples.english: Unfortunately, I was seriously injured in an accident.

examples.japanese: {不幸中|ふこうちゅう}の{幸|さいわ}いで、{命|いのち}に{別状|べつじょう}はなかった。
examples.english: As a silver lining, there was no danger to life.
examples.notes: 不幸中の幸い = a blessing in disguise, silver lining

examples.japanese: {家族|かぞく}に{不幸|ふこう}があり、{欠席|けっせき}します。
examples.english: I will be absent due to a death in the family.
examples.notes: Euphemism for death in the family

examples.japanese: {不幸|ふこう}があったので、{旅行|りょこう}は{中止|ちゅうし}にした。
examples.english: There was a death in the family, so I canceled the trip.

examples.japanese: {同僚|どうりょう}のご{家族|かぞく}に{不幸|ふこう}があったと{聞|き}いて、お{悔|く}やみの{言葉|ことば}を{伝|つた}えた。
examples.english: I heard that there was a death in a colleague's family and offered my condolences.

notes:
USAGE: {不幸|ふこう} can describe general unhappiness, bad luck, or serve as a polite euphemism for death in the family.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{不幸|ふこう}な{出来事|できごと} (unfortunate event)
・{不幸|ふこう}に{見舞|みま}われる (to be struck by misfortune)
・{不幸|ふこう}にも (unfortunately)
・{不幸中|ふこうちゅう}の{幸|さいわ}い (a silver lining)

ANTONYM: {幸福|こうふく} (happiness)
